root_cause.text: In the SMB client’s `struct cached_fid`, the `is_open`, `has_lease`, and `on_list` flags were packed into the same bitfield byte, so concurrent updates from different code paths could race via byte-wide read-modify-write stores and inadvertently restore stale flag values.
root_cause.evidence: The patch and CVE description explicitly say these three fields “are stored in the same bitfield byte” and that “bitfield assignments generate byte read–modify–write operations,” allowing an interleaving where one CPU clears flags while another CPU’s RMW store reintroduces them; the fix is to “convert these flags to separate bool fields” in `fs/smb/client/cached_dir.h`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert packed boolean bitfields in `struct cached_fid` to regular booleans, changing layout without altering flag semantics.
intent_record.what: In struct cached_fid, the four bitfield boolean members `has_lease`, `is_open`, `on_list`, and `file_all_info_is_valid` were changed from `bool:1` bitfields to plain `bool` fields. No other code in the hunk was modified.
intent_record.how: This changes the in-memory layout of `struct cached_fid` by storing each flag as a full boolean value instead of a packed one-bit field. Runtime semantics of the flags themselves remain the same, but the structure may now have different size, alignment, and access characteristics, which can affect memory usage and ABI/layout assumptions.
